docs.title: Cobblemon Champions Training
docs.text:
Effort values step aside for stat points, the way Pokémon Champions does it. A Pokémon no longer soaks up EVs from whatever it happens to knock out: you decide what it becomes, you train it at a Champions Trainer NPC, and you pay for it yourself.

MC 1.21.1 Fabric NeoForge Cobblemon 1.8

Get started Stat points

docs.title: What can it do?
docs.text:
• Champions Trainer: the NPC in every PokeTowns Pokémon Center where changes are bought. The summary shows your build anywhere.
  • Stat points: up to 32 in a stat and 66 in total, each worth +1 to the stat at any level. They are spent on the summary's stats page.
  • Nature, ability and moves: change the nature and the ability on the summary's info page, and switch to any move the Pokémon can legally learn.
  • Saved sets: keep four builds per Pokémon and load a whole one in two clicks.
  • Training costs: everything is paid with your own experience, or with CobbleDollars on servers that want it.
  • Commands & Config: every system can be switched off and every price tuned, in game.

docs.title: Get it
docs.text:
Download Modrinth · CurseForge · What changed Version 2.0.0 Minecraft 1.21.1 Side Server and every player's game Cobblemon 1.8 — 1.7.3 is not supported Fabric Fabric Language Kotlin NeoForge Kotlin for Forge Optional Cobblemon: PlayerXP: experience for the battles you win · CobbleDollars: a second currency · Cloth Config: the settings screen (with Mod Menu on Fabric) · Cobblemon PokeTowns: puts a Champions Trainer in every Pokémon Center

New here? Start with Getting Started.

docs.title: Champions Trainer
docs.text:
From version 2.0.0, everything this mod sells can be tied to a Champions Trainer, an NPC that stands in the world. That covers stat points, loading a saved set, the nature, the ability and the moves of a Pokémon in training. Where a trainer is required, the summary screen still shows all of it anywhere you open it. It just doesn't sell anything on its own.

Prices are the same as before. Training Costs lists them.

docs.title: When a trainer is required
docs.text:
It depends on PokeTowns:

Where changes are bought PokeTowns installed At a Champions Trainer. One stands in every Pokémon Center. No PokeTowns From the summary, anywhere, as before 2.0.0. A trainer still works if an operator places one.

An operator can override this either way with a command, which is saved to the config file:

/champions config trainer required on      always at a trainer
/champions config trainer required off     always from the summary
/champions config trainer required auto    back to the default above

docs.title: Where to find one
docs.text:
With PokeTowns, every Pokémon Center has a Champions Trainer standing beside the counter, three blocks along from Nurse Joy. It appears the first time the Center loads, so Centers in a world generated before this update get one too.

If an operator removes a Center's trainer, it does not come back. To stop placing them at all, use /champions config trainer inCenters false. Trainers already placed stay.

docs.title: Placing a trainer
docs.text:
The trainer is a regular Cobblemon NPC, so an operator can place one anywhere with Cobblemon's own command:

/spawnnpc cobblemon_champions_training:champions_trainer

It does not despawn, cannot be hurt, and stays where it was placed across restarts. Cobblemon's NPC tools (/npcedit, /npcdelete, the NPC editor item in creative) work on it like on any other NPC. On a server, put one wherever players should go to train, such as a gym.

docs.title: Training at the trainer
docs.text:
1. Walk up to the trainer and talk to it (right click).
  2. Your party's summary opens, with every training control live: SP, Sets → Load, the Nature and Ability pickers on the Info page, and the move screen on Moves.
  3. Buy what you want, exactly as described in Stat Points, Saved Sets and Nature, Ability & Moves.
  4. Close the summary when you are done. Talk to the trainer again to keep training.

If you have no Pokémon with you, the trainer says to come back when you do.

docs.title: Away from a trainer
docs.text:
Where a trainer is required, open the summary anywhere else (with the summary key, or from the PC) and you can still read everything, but you can't change it:

  • On SP, the +, −, ++, Save and Reset buttons are greyed out and the footer says Visit a Champions Trainer to change this Pokémon.
  • On Sets, Load is greyed out the same way. Store, Delete and renaming a set still work, because a set is only a note kept on your own computer.
  • On Info, the Nature and Ability rows have no ▼ and don't open.
  • On Moves, the move screen does not open for a Pokémon in training, and a notice says to visit a trainer. Reordering moves still works.

A Pokémon that is not in training (below 31 in every IV) is untouched: its summary and its moves are plain Cobblemon everywhere.

docs.title: Distance
docs.text: The server checks every purchase, not just the screen. You have to be in the same world as the trainer that opened the summary and within 8 blocks of it. If you walk away, or the trainer is removed, the next purchase is refused with the same Visit a Champions Trainer message. Talk to a trainer again to carry on.

docs.title: Server notes
docs.text:
• With "Moves come from" set to Cobblemon's list, free, the mod leaves moves alone and the move screen works anywhere, as in plain Cobblemon. The other two settings put move changes at the trainer too. See the settings.
  • Mints, Ability Capsules and Ability Patches are items, not summary controls. They follow their own settings and are not tied to the trainer.
  • Every player who trains needs the mod on their client. On a client without it, the trainer does nothing.

docs.title: Commands & Config
docs.text: Every system this mod replaces can be switched off, and every price can be changed. Do it from the config screen, from /champions config in game, or in the settings file.

docs.title: Placing a Champions Trainer
docs.text: /spawnnpc cobblemon_champions_training:champions_trainer, for an operator. This is Cobblemon's own command. With PokeTowns, every Pokémon Center already has one. See Champions Trainer.

docs.title: /champions sp [slot]
docs.text:
A read-out of one party Pokémon, for anyone. slot is 1 to 6, counted the way your party screen counts, and defaults to 1.

=== Bulbasaur (slot 1, level 30) ===
Gate: open — Champions training is available.
Budget: 66/66
HP sp=32 room=0 ev=0 iv=31 • stat=97
Attack sp=32 room=0 ev=0 iv=31 • stat=81
...
Line What it tells you Gate Whether the Pokémon is in training. When it is not, which IVs are short of 31, with their values. Budget Points in use, out of 66 one line per stat Its stat points (sp), how many more it can take (room), its effort values and IV, and the final stat

Running it also switches a Pokémon over if it has just reached 31 in every IV, so its numbers are the ones you will be spending. When stat points are turned off on the server, it says so first.

docs.title: /champions config
docs.text:
For operators (permission level 2). Every change is saved to the settings file and reaches every connected player at once; nobody has to reconnect.

/champions config                               every setting, grouped
/champions config <group>                       one group
/champions config <group> <setting>             one value
/champions config <group> <setting> <value>     change it
/champions config <group> reset [<setting>]     back to the default
/champions config reset_all                     every setting back to its default

A value that is not one of the allowed ones is refused, and the message lists the ones that are. Typing a group name and pressing Tab suggests its settings.

docs.title: The settings
docs.text:
Group Setting Values Default What it controls statpoints enabled true / false true The stat-point system. Off: effort values as in plain Cobblemon, points kept for later. statpoints requireMaxIvs true / false true Only a Pokémon with 31 in every IV can train. statpoints hyperTrainingUnlocks true / false true IVs raised with Bottle Caps count toward the 31s. statpoints xpPerStatPoint 0 or more 10 Experience per stat point moved. nature source MINTS / TRAINING / BOTH BOTH Where a nature can be changed: mints, the Info page, or both. nature xpPerNatureChange 0 or more 1000 Experience per nature. ability source ITEMS / TRAINING / BOTH BOTH Where an ability can be changed: Ability Capsules and Patches, the Info page, or both. ability xpPerAbilityChange 0 or more 2000 Experience per ability. ability xpPerHiddenAbility 0 or more 6000 Experience per hidden ability. moves source SWAP / TRAINING / BOTH BOTH SWAP: Cobblemon's list, free. TRAINING: every legal move, charged. BOTH: every legal move, free. moves xpPerMoveChange 0 or more 500 Experience per move, when moves are charged. moves xpPerEggMove 0 or more 1500 Experience per egg move, when moves are charged. currency order XP_ONLY / XP_THEN_COBBLEDOLLARS / COBBLEDOLLARS_THEN_XP / COBBLEDOLLARS_ONLY XP_ONLY What training is paid in. currency rate 1 or more 10 Experience per CobbleDollar, rounded up. trainer required AUTO / ON / OFF AUTO Whether changes are bought only at a Champions Trainer. AUTO: only with PokeTowns installed. trainer inCenters true / false true A trainer is placed in every PokeTowns Pokémon Center. Does nothing without PokeTowns.

For example, to charge for moves and make egg moves steeper:

/champions config moves source TRAINING
/champions config moves xpPerEggMove 3000

Nature, Ability & Moves and Training Costs explain what these do in play.

docs.title: The config screen
docs.text:
With Cloth Config installed, the same settings are on a screen: on Fabric, open it from Mod Menu; on NeoForge, from the mods list. Each setting has a tooltip.

Whose settings count

The server's settings are the rules. While you are connected to a server, your game uses the server's values, whatever your own file says, and it goes back to yours when you leave. The screen always edits your own file, which is what counts in single player and on a server you host.

docs.title: The settings file
docs.text:
config/cobblemon_champions_training.json, created with the defaults the first time the game starts.

{
  "configVersion": 1,
  "statPointsEnabled": true,
  "requireMaxIvs": true,
  "hyperTrainingUnlocks": true,
  "natureSource": "BOTH",
  "abilitySource": "BOTH",
  "moveSource": "BOTH",
  "xpPerStatPoint": 10,
  "xpPerNatureChange": 1000,
  "xpPerAbilityChange": 2000,
  "xpPerHiddenAbility": 6000,
  "xpPerMoveChange": 500,
  "xpPerEggMove": 1500,
  "costOrder": "XP_ONLY",
  "xpPerCobbleDollar": 10,
  "trainerRequired": "AUTO",
  "trainerInCenters": true
}

A missing key takes its default, and a misspelled value falls back to the default with a line in the log naming the key and the values it accepts. A negative price is read as 0, and a rate under 1 as 1.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Cobblemon Champions Training goes on both sides: the server keeps the rules and the points, and your game draws the pages you train from. In single player, that is just your own mods/ folder.

Drop one jar, the one for your loader, never both.

FabricNeoForge Minecraft 1.21.1 Required Cobblemon 1.8 and what it needs (Fabric Language Kotlin, Architectury API) Recommended Cobblemon: PlayerXP Optional CobbleDollars · Cloth Config + Mod Menu for the settings screen Minecraft 1.21.1 Required Cobblemon 1.8 and what it needs (Kotlin for Forge, Architectury API) Recommended Cobblemon: PlayerXP Optional CobbleDollars · Cloth Config for the settings screen

Why PlayerXP

Training is paid with your experience. Vanilla only pays experience for defeating mobs, and a Cobblemon world has little of that. PlayerXP pays you for the battles your Pokémon win, so what training spends refills from what you are already doing.

docs.title: Which Pokémon it touches
docs.text:
Only a Pokémon that is 31 in all six IVs. It can get there by being bred that way, caught that way, or raised with Bottle Caps. Everything below that is plain Cobblemon: its stats, its effort values and its summary screen are exactly the game's own.

The moment a Pokémon crosses that line, it switches over once and for good, and you see:

This Pokémon trains with stat points now — open its summary to spend them. Effort values no longer do anything for it.

Where a Champions Trainer is required, it says visit a Champions Trainer instead.

Whatever effort values it had become its first stat points, so a Pokémon you trained before is not set back. Stat Points explains the exchange.

A server can loosen or tighten this rule, or turn the stat points off entirely; see Commands & Config.

docs.title: Where everything is
docs.text:
Everything is on the Pokémon's summary. There is no new screen and no new item. Since version 2.0.0, with PokeTowns installed, the summary only sells at a Champions Trainer, who stands in every Pokémon Center: talk to one and its summary opens with every control live. Opened anywhere else, it shows the same pages read-only. Without PokeTowns, the summary sells anywhere unless the server asks for a trainer.

Summary page What changes Details Stats The IV and EV tabs are replaced by SP and Sets Stat Points · Saved Sets Info The Nature and Ability rows open a picker, marked with a ▼ Nature, Ability & Moves Moves Cobblemon's move screen offers every move the Pokémon can legally learn Nature, Ability & Moves

Every change shows its price before you commit to it, is paid once, and plays a short chime when it goes through. Training Costs lists the prices.

docs.title: Your first build
docs.text:
1. Open the summary, or talk to a Champions Trainer if your server asks for one. Pick a Pokémon with 31 in every IV and go to Stats → SP.
  2. Use + and − to spread up to 66 points, 32 at most in one stat. ++ fills a stat as far as it can go.
  3. Read the price under the buttons, then press Save.
  4. On the Info page, click the Nature row, pick the stat to raise and the stat to lower, and press Train.
  5. Back on Stats → Sets, press Store on an empty slot. The whole build is saved, ready to load again later.

docs.title: Nature, Ability & Moves
docs.text: Stat points are half of a build. The other half is changed where you already read it: the nature and the ability on the summary's Info page, and the moves on Cobblemon's own move screen. All three are changed in a summary opened by a Champions Trainer.

docs.title: The Info page
docs.text:
On a Pokémon in training, the Nature and Ability rows carry a small ▼ at their right edge. Click the row to open its picker.

A row only has the marker when it really opens:

  • the summary was opened by a Champions Trainer;
  • the Pokémon is in training (31 in every IV);
  • the server lets training change that thing (see the settings);
  • for the ability, the Pokémon's form has more than one ability to choose from.

Everywhere else the page is exactly Cobblemon's. Click outside the picker to close it without buying.

docs.title: Nature
docs.text:
The nature picker has three parts: the stat to raise (+), the stat to lower (−), and the nature those two make.

Raise Lower Nature Attack Speed Brave Attack Sp. Atk Adamant Speed Attack Timid Sp. Atk Attack Modest

HP is not on either side, because no nature touches it. Picking the same stat on both sides gives the neutral nature that sits on that line of the nature table:

Raise and lower Neutral nature Attack Hardy Defence Docile Sp. Atk Bashful Sp. Def Quirky Speed Serious

The picker opens on the nature the Pokémon has now. The line under it shows what the chosen nature does and its price; press Train to buy it.

The nature you buy is layered over the one the Pokémon was born with, just as a mint does. Picking its birth nature again removes that layer.

docs.title: Ability
docs.text:
The ability picker lists every ability the Pokémon's form can have, its hidden ability included. The highlighted one's description is shown under the list, and a hidden ability is marked as such. A hidden ability costs more than a common one, because it is something players breed for.

Pick one and press Train.

docs.title: Moves
docs.text:
A Pokémon in training can switch to any move its form can legally learn: level-up moves, TMs, tutor moves and egg moves. The switch happens on Cobblemon's own move screen, where the full list appears; nothing new to learn.

"Moves come from" Moves offered Cost of a switch Every legal move, free (default) the whole learnset nothing Every legal move, charged the whole learnset the move's price; egg moves cost more Cobblemon's list, free only the moves it already learned nothing, as in plain Cobblemon

Under the first two settings, the move screen of a Pokémon in training only opens at a Champions Trainer. Under Cobblemon's list, free it works anywhere.

Putting the same moves in a different order is never charged. Levelling up still teaches moves as usual, whatever the setting.

TMs

A Pokémon in training can already switch to every move a TM would teach, so a TM tells you it already knows the move and is not used up.

docs.title: Mints, Ability Capsules and Ability Patches
docs.text:
They keep working by default. A server can make nature or ability changes training only, and then a mint, a capsule or a patch does nothing and says so; with mints only or capsules and patches only, the pickers on the Info page stay closed instead.

Prices are on Training Costs; the settings are on Commands & Config.

docs.title: Saved Sets
docs.text: A set is a whole build: a Pokémon's stat points, nature, ability and four moves. Each Pokémon keeps four of them, on the Sets tab of its summary's Stats page, next to SP. Load spends, so it only works at a Champions Trainer; storing, naming and deleting a set work anywhere.

docs.title: The four slots
docs.text:
Each row is a slot, numbered 1 to 4. A slot shows the name you gave it, or, until you name it, its two biggest stats (Atk 32 · Spe 32). An empty slot says — empty —.

Click a row to select it. The buttons under the list act on the selected slot:

Selected slot Buttons Empty Store Saved Load and Delete

A saved set is never written over. To save a different build in its place, delete it first.

docs.title: Store
docs.text: Saves the Pokémon as it is: the stat points it has bought, its current nature and ability, and its moves. Changes still waiting on the SP tab's Save are not part of it.

docs.title: Load
docs.text:
Puts the whole set on the Pokémon at once: stat points, nature, ability and moves.

  1. Select the set. Its price appears under the buttons.
  2. Press Load. It turns into Sure?.
  3. Press it again. The server checks the set, charges the price once and applies everything, and a chime confirms it. Any unsaved changes on the SP tab are dropped.

Load stays grey when:

  • the set is already exactly what the Pokémon has;
  • you cannot afford it;
  • it uses a move this Pokémon cannot learn, or an ability it cannot have, for example after it evolved into a different form;
  • it asks for more points than a stat or the budget can hold.

For the last three, the reason is written under the buttons.

A set is never loaded in part. The one exception is a part the server does not let you train: on a server where natures only come from mints, a set still loads its points, ability and moves, and leaves the nature alone.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text: Press Delete. It turns into Sure?; press it again to empty the slot, name and all. Clicking anything else in between cancels it.

docs.title: Naming a set
docs.text: Click the name of the slot that is already selected, type, and press Enter. Escape cancels and Backspace deletes. A name holds up to 18 characters. Every key goes to the name while you type, so the letter that normally closes the summary does not.

docs.title: Reading a set without loading it
docs.text:
Rest the cursor on a saved slot. The tooltip lists:

  • its six stat points and their total;
  • its nature, with the stat it raises in green and the one it lowers in red;
  • its ability;
  • its moves, each in its type's colour.

Hovering an empty slot shows nothing.

docs.title: Where sets are kept
docs.text:
On your computer, in config/cobblemon_champions_training_profiles.json, filed under each Pokémon. They are not stored on the server, so another computer does not have them. The file keeps sets for up to 64 Pokémon; past that, the Pokémon whose sets changed longest ago is dropped.

Training Costs has what a set costs to load.

docs.title: Stat Points
docs.text: A Pokémon in training has stat points where it used to have effort values. They follow the Pokémon Champions standard: a small budget you spend on purpose, instead of a number that piles up from whatever the Pokémon knocked out.

docs.title: The numbers
docs.text:
Effort values Stat points Most in one stat 252 32 Most in total 510 66 Worth, per unit depends on the level +1 to the stat, at any level Earned by defeating Pokémon buying them, on the SP tab

A point is added to the stat before the nature is applied, so a nature that raises a stat raises the points in it too. HP takes its points as they are.

Because a point is always +1, the same 32 points add the same amount to a Pokémon at level 5 as at level 100.

docs.title: Converting from effort values
docs.text:
A Pokémon switches over once, the first time it is 31 in every IV. Its effort values are read as points it had already spent, at the same rate Pokémon HOME uses: the first point in a stat is worth 4 effort values, and every point after that is worth 8.

Effort values in a stat Stat points 0–3 0 4 1 12 2 252 32

A classic 252 / 252 / 6 spread becomes 32 / 32 / 1: 65 points, one under the budget. When a Pokémon brings more than 66 points' worth, the biggest stats are kept first and the smallest are trimmed.

It switches over whenever the game next looks at it:

  • when it hatches or joins your party (caught, traded, given);
  • when Bottle Caps raise its last IV to 31;
  • the first time it would earn effort values in battle;
  • the first time you train it: Save, Train or Load.

Once it has switched:

  • it never earns effort values again;
  • its moves are always at their full PP, including the moves it learns by levelling up.

Bottle Caps

By default, IVs raised with Bottle Caps count toward the 31s. A server can make only natural IVs count; a Pokémon that already switched over with Bottle Caps stays in.

docs.title: The SP tab
docs.text:
Open the Pokémon's summary, go to Stats, and pick SP, where the EV tab used to be. The buttons only work in a summary opened by a Champions Trainer; anywhere else the tab shows the points with the buttons greyed out.

Control What it does SP x / 66 Points in use, out of the budget − / + Take a point off a stat, or put one on ++ Fill the stat as far as it can go, within 32 and what is left of the 66 the bar under each stat How full that stat is, out of 32 Reset Take every point off Save Buy the whole change at once

Nothing is spent while you click −, +, ++ and Reset: you are editing a draft. The price of the whole draft appears under Save. Taking a point off costs the same as putting one on, because what you pay for is the change; moving a point from Attack to Speed is two changes.

  • If you cannot afford the draft, the price turns red, the reason is written under it, and Save stays grey.
  • After you press Save, the button greys out until you change something, and a chime confirms the purchase.

The summary's stats reflect the new points straight away, and they are there the next time you open it. Training Costs has the prices.

docs.title: When a server changes the rules
docs.text:
Setting Effect on stat points Stat points off Every Pokémon uses and earns effort values as in plain Cobblemon, and the summary shows its own IV and EV tabs. Points already spent are kept, and come back as they were when this is turned on again. Require perfect IVs off Every Pokémon can train, whatever its IVs. Bottle Caps unlock training off Only natural IVs count toward the 31s.

A Pokémon already over its budget can always save a spread that uses fewer points, never one that uses more. See Commands & Config for how to change these.

docs.title: Training Costs
docs.text: Training is something the trainer pays for. Every change is paid out of your own experience bar, not the Pokémon's, so rebuilding a team is an investment and a mistake is a real one.

docs.title: The price list
docs.text:
These are the defaults. A server can change every one of them, and a price of 0 makes that step free.

Change Price (experience points) One stat point, up or down 10 A nature 1,000 An ability 2,000 The hidden ability 6,000 A move 500, only when the server charges for moves An egg move 1,500, only when the server charges for moves

The ratios come from the Pokémon Champions standard, where a move costs 50 stat points, a nature 100 and an ability 200. The hidden ability and egg moves cost three times more, because those are what players breed for, and breeding should stay the cheaper road.

  • Stat points are charged per point moved, in both directions: taking one off costs the same as putting one on. The whole draft on the SP tab is paid once, on Save.
  • Moves are free by default. The server's "Moves come from" setting decides; see Nature, Ability & Moves. Putting moves in a different order is never charged.
  • Loading a set costs what its parts cost together (the stat points that change, plus a nature, ability or moves that differ), and is paid once.

Prices are quoted in experience points, not levels: Costs 640 experience. A level is worth more experience the higher you are, so the same purchase takes more of a low-level bar than a high one.

docs.title: Currency
docs.text:
By default everything is paid in experience. A server with CobbleDollars (CurseForge) can bill in its money instead.

"Paid in" What happens Experience only (default) Always experience Experience, then CobbleDollars Experience if you have enough, otherwise CobbleDollars CobbleDollars, then experience CobbleDollars if you have enough, otherwise experience CobbleDollars only Always CobbleDollars
  • A price is never split between the two: one currency pays the whole of it.
  • Prices stay written in experience and are converted at the server's rate, 10 experience per CobbleDollar by default, rounded up. A 500-experience move costs 50 CobbleDollars.
  • Without CobbleDollars installed, everything is paid in experience, whatever the setting says.

Whenever CobbleDollars can pay, the page cannot see your balance, so the buttons stay live and the server is the one that decides whether you can afford it.

docs.title: Where the experience comes from
docs.text:
Vanilla Minecraft only pays experience for defeating mobs, and a Cobblemon world has little of that. Cobblemon: PlayerXP (CurseForge) pays you experience for the battles your Pokémon win, so what training spends refills from what you are already doing. It is recommended, not required.

Changing a price is on Commands & Config.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common surprises, what causes them, and what to do. If yours is not here, post it in the Discord: it files the ticket for you.

docs.title: Nothing changed on my Pokémon
docs.text: The mod only touches a Pokémon that is 31 in all six IVs. Everything below that is plain Cobblemon. Breed, catch or raise it there with Bottle Caps; see Which Pokémon it touches.

docs.title: I keep running out of experience for training
docs.text: Training is paid with your experience, and vanilla only pays experience for defeating mobs. Cobblemon: PlayerXP pays you for the battles your Pokémon win. See Training Costs.

docs.title: My settings screen changes do nothing on a server
docs.text: While you are connected to a server, your game uses the server's values, whatever your own file says. The screen always edits your own file, which is what counts in single player and on a server you host. See The config screen.

docs.title: Does it run on Cobblemon 1.7.3?
docs.text: No. Champions Training is built for Cobblemon 1.8 and 1.7.3 is not supported.
